subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which condition is REQUIRED for a tropical storm to form?
options: Sea-surface temperatures of at least about 27 degrees C
questions.explain: Tropical storms need warm ocean water of around 27 degrees C or more to provide energy.

questions.q: Many scientists predict climate change will make tropical storms:
options: Move towards the poles and stop
questions.explain: Warmer oceans give storms more energy, so they are expected to become more intense.

questions.q: The calm, clear centre of a tropical storm is called the:
questions.explain: The eye is the calm low-pressure centre, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

questions.q: The Saffir-Simpson scale is used to measure the:
options: Strength of tropical storms by wind speed
questions.explain: The Saffir-Simpson scale rates tropical storms from category 1 to 5 by their wind speeds.

questions.q: Tropical storms are called hurricanes in the:
options: Atlantic and east Pacific (e.g. the Caribbean)
questions.explain: The same storm is a hurricane in the Atlantic/east Pacific, a typhoon in the west Pacific and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: In the Hadley cell, air at the equator rises because it is:
options: Warm and rising, creating low pressure
questions.explain: Intense equatorial heating makes air rise, forming a low-pressure belt with heavy rain.

questions.q: Which is a NATURAL cause of climate change?
options: Variations in the Sun's output and volcanic eruptions
questions.explain: Solar variation, orbital changes and volcanic activity are natural climate drivers.

questions.q: An example of an extreme UK weather hazard is:
options: Heavy snow, flooding and winter storms
A tropical cyclone forming over Britain
questions.explain: The UK experiences hazards such as flooding, storms, heatwaves and heavy snow.

questions.q: A tropical storm usually loses energy and weakens when it:
options: Moves over land or cooler water
questions.explain: Cut off from warm ocean moisture over land or cool seas, the storm loses its energy source and weakens.

questions.q: In which atmospheric cell does cold air sink at the poles, creating high pressure?
questions.explain: In the Polar cell, very cold dense air sinks at the poles forming high pressure.

questions.q: Which is an example of PLANNING to reduce tropical storm impacts?
options: Educating people on evacuation routes and storm drills
questions.explain: Preparation such as evacuation plans and public education reduces casualties when storms strike.

questions.q: A storm surge during a tropical storm is:
options: A sudden rise in sea level that floods coastal areas
questions.explain: Low pressure and powerful winds push seawater onshore, raising sea level and flooding the coast.

questions.q: Which is a PRIMARY effect of a tropical storm?
options: Disease spreading from contaminated water afterwards
Buildings destroyed directly by strong winds
Loss of tourism income months later
questions.explain: Wind damage to buildings happens directly during the storm, making it a primary effect.

questions.q: The most intense winds and heaviest rain in a tropical storm occur in the:
questions.explain: The eyewall, the ring of towering clouds around the eye, has the strongest winds and rain.

questions.q: Tropical storms generally do NOT form right at the equator because:
options: The sea is too warm there
There is too little Coriolis effect to make them spin
questions.explain: The Coriolis effect is near zero at the equator, so storms cannot start spinning.

questions.q: Which is an example of ADAPTATION to climate change?
options: Using solar panels instead of coal
Building sea walls to cope with rising sea levels
questions.explain: Adaptation means coping with effects, such as defending coasts against higher seas.

questions.q: Which is an example of MITIGATION of climate change rather than adaptation?
options: Switching to renewable energy to cut emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions); adaptation copes with the effects.

questions.q: The greenhouse effect becomes a problem for climate when:
options: Extra greenhouse gases trap more heat, warming the planet
questions.explain: Higher concentrations of greenhouse gases trap additional heat, enhancing warming.

questions.q: Which gas released by burning fossil fuels is the main HUMAN cause of recent climate change?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the chief human-enhanced greenhouse gas.

questions.q: Which is the strongest piece of EVIDENCE for recent climate change?
options: Rising global average temperatures and shrinking ice sheets
questions.explain: Records of rising temperatures, melting ice and sea-level rise evidence climate change.

questions.q: At around 30 degrees north and south, air in the global circulation:
options: Sinks, creating high pressure and deserts
questions.explain: Sinking air at roughly 30 degrees forms high pressure and the world's hot deserts.

questions.q: Surface winds blowing towards the equator from the high-pressure belts are called the:
questions.explain: Trade winds blow from the subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Geography (B) (J384) specification; Changing Climate
